root.label: System composition root
root.purpose: src/cli.ts → src/app.ts + configuration assemble the deployment. Cordis resolves dependencies and owns plugin lifecycle. The root wires capabilities together; it does not own research decisions.

layers.label: Primitives
layers.purpose: Store bytes and records; verify account identity.

layers.label: Authority & durable events
layers.purpose: Turn primitives into project permissions, protected credentials and reliable events.

layers.label: Shared platform capabilities
layers.purpose: Reusable objects, repositories, callable operations and workflow state.

layers.label: Execution & context
layers.purpose: Allocate workers, authorize sessions, assemble context and record activity.

layers.label: Domain & agent capabilities
layers.purpose: Build reviewed research documents, research Git operations and interactive agents.

layers.label: Research work
layers.purpose: Use the platform to deliver tasks and execute reviewed experiments.

layers.label: Project knowledge & synthesis
layers.purpose: Read across work and turn completed evidence into reviewed reflection.

layers.label: Research coordination

boundaries.label: External service adapters

boundaries.label: Execution bindings
boundaries.purpose: Fleet Workflow binds dispatch to hosting. Runner executes on a separate machine. These connect execution boundaries.

boundaries.label: HTTP / MCP boundary
boundaries.purpose: API and route adapters expose existing capabilities. They are not a research layer.

boundaries.label: Agent tool adapters

boundaries.label: Browser UI & adapters
boundaries.purpose: Present domain capabilities. The UI shell and its views sit beside the stack.

groups.label: Front door
groups.caption: HTTP, MCP & the browser
groups.description: API accepts requests, Tools controls the callable catalog, and UI hosts the browser. Small adapters connect these registries to the domain plugins.

groups.label: Identity
groups.caption: Shared user login
groups.description: Identity verifies shared users. Scope owns project membership, permissions and tool policy. External Mounts owns upstream credential selection.

groups.label: Integrations
groups.caption: Remote tools, compute & search
groups.description: External Mounts connects independent MCP servers to the local tool registry. Sandboxes connects directly to the remote compute service over HTTP, publishing its views and lease controls. Web searches the internet through Tavily, with OpenAI's hosted web search as its fallback, and Nisa searches the literature through RapidReview's paper index. Each integration owns its upstream credentials; availability is not proof of remote health.

groups.label: Research
groups.caption: The work & what we learn
groups.description: Research workflows own scientific work, its context recipes and paper edit proposals. Paper stores the reviewed documents; Knowledge assembles source records. Research keeps its State/Scope/Workflows core active and binds its stage providers optionally. Digests read selected Tasks and Experiments directly. Only stages that use a missing provider wait. Accepted code missing from main is integrated through a reviewed Git task using Code Work.

groups.label: Coordination
groups.caption: Gates, agents & code
groups.description: Workflows evaluates gates and assignments. Agent Sessions controls worker authority and recovery. Code retains requests and exact code-capture references. The separate Runner performs machine work.

groups.label: Evidence
groups.caption: Files, reviews & context
groups.description: Artifacts owns file metadata. Reviews retains independent assessments. Context Builder assembles the domain's context recipe. Feed records project activity.

groups.label: External services
groups.caption: Connected over MCP / HTTP
groups.description: Nisa and the Sandboxes compute service run independently. Optional MCP mounts expose remote tools; the local Sandboxes plugin also connects to the compute service over HTTP.

groups.label: Foundation
groups.caption: Shared durable capabilities
groups.description: State and Scope are the most shared dependencies. Blobs stores bytes without depending on State; Artifacts connects file metadata to those bytes. Domain Events reads durable events from State.

groups.label: Separate machine
groups.caption: Agents & Git checkouts
groups.description: Runner has its own Cordis context. It talks to the server over authenticated HTTP and launches scoped agents in scratch or Git workspaces. It has no injected server-plugin dependencies.

groups.label: New providers
groups.caption: Discovered in source
groups.description: These providers were discovered automatically and await a visual grouping in notes.json.

exposedTools.name: code.commit
exposedTools.description: Request a Git checkpoint of this active writable session’s assigned checkout. Read its current HEAD with local Git first. Supply that full expectedHead, a commit message and a stable requestId. The message has a fixed shape: a first line of at most 72 characters saying what changed, then a blank line and, only where there is more than one thing to say, up to ten bullet points (each a line beginning "- "), one per significant change, each short. No paragraphs, no restated task, no session or commit ids. The owning runner performs fixed Git operations; this does not publish central or submit a proposal. It commits what the checkout holds and stages, ignored paths aside; a new or changed file over 50 MiB fails the operation, so keep such data out of Git. Returns a durable operation. If queued or dispatched, inspect code.operation with the returned command.id. Reusing the same request with different input is refused. The runner also commits this checkout by itself every five minutes ("Checkpoint: …"), which moves HEAD: an expectedHead that only those checkpoints have moved past is taken as the newest of them, so the commit lands on top of them. An operation that failed with workspace_head_conflict means HEAD moved after you read it: read it again and commit under a new requestId.

exposedTools.name: code.merge
exposedTools.description: Start materializes the frozen merge in a clean checkout. Complete commits its resolution with the current checkpoint and frozen second parent. Supply expectedHead, message and a stable requestId; poll code.operation for the receipt. The message has a fixed shape: a first line of at most 72 characters saying what changed, then a blank line and, only where there is more than one thing to say, up to ten bullet points (each a line beginning "- "), one per significant change, each short. No paragraphs, no restated task, no session or commit ids.

exposedTools.name: code.publication.read
exposedTools.description: Read one integration with its pull request as GitHub has it now: the files, commits, reviews and checks. Merv’s pages read it; agents use code.status.

exposedTools.name: fleet
exposedTools.description:
The project’s Fleet allocations: the machines its workers run on.
list: open allocations and the 50 latest ended ones, with machine lifecycle status.
get: one allocation by id; a requested shutdown is distinct from confirmed machine deletion.
drain: stop admission on id, keep the current assignment’s results, then release its machine (its source or a project administrator).
halt: fence id and request immediate machine deletion; in-flight work may be interrupted (its source or a project administrator).
project_limit: how many machines the project may run at once; machines sets it (a project administrator or their agent).
workflow_retry_status: why Fleet stopped renting for one workflow revision (instanceId, expectedRevision) after unclaimed machines.
workflow_retry: open one more two-attempt window for that revision (project administrator; reason, stable requestId).

nodes.label: Knowledge
nodes.purpose: Composes live project, task and experiment records and resolves scoped artifact, review, workflow and code references through their owning services. It has no writable research corpus or publication workflow. Its tool adapter exposes project.records and project.references independently of Research.

exposedTools.name: project.records
exposedTools.description: Index the project: its id and name, then one short entry per task and experiment (state, review, deliveries, conclusion), terminal work included. Pass ids (up to 20 task or experiment ids) to get those records whole instead, with every attempt, evidence association, submission and delivery confirmation; ids that are neither come back in missing. task.get and experiment.get_state read one record whole. The project Introduction is the Problem of the paper, which paper.read returns. Does not read artifact bytes or advance workflows. To resolve other ids to labels and states use project.references; gate, blockers and next actions use workflow.status_and_next.

exposedTools.name: project.references
exposedTools.description: Resolve up to 200 project-scoped references to exact record metadata. Accepts record IDs or task:, experiment:, reflection:, research:, artifact:, review:, code-commit: and session-final: followed by an ID. Each result explicitly identifies resolved, missing or unsupported references; a bare ID is unavailable while a service that might hold it is restarting. Does not read artifact bytes.

nodes.label: Nisa
nodes.purpose: Searches the scholarly literature for every agent through Nisa's public API: keyword and semantic search, one paper's record, passages inside its full text, and similar papers, each named the way paper.cite takes it. Its tools are open-world reads with one deployment-wide key. Composed only where that key is configured; it has no injected Cordis dependencies.

exposedTools.name: nisa.read
exposedTools.description: Read Nisa's arXiv index: search (by keyword), semantic_search (by meaning), paper (one paper's record), excerpts (passages of one paper matching terms), related (similar papers) and status (a research operation started with nisa.write, and its report). Queries leave Merv for Nisa.

exposedTools.name: nisa.research
exposedTools.description: Delegate a full research brief directly to Nisa’s research agent, investigators and reporter (GPT-6.1 Sol), bypassing general chat. Include goals, context, prior papers, scope and desired evidence. start creates a retained conversation; follow_up builds on its research. Both require a stable request_id: reuse it on retries. Returns operation_id and conversation_id immediately. Poll status using operation_id (about every 15 seconds); cancel stops that operation. Page long reports using answer_offset/next_answer_offset. Shared Merv account pays; bounded research allowance is separate from your own model budget. Only your scoped conversations are accessible. Never send credentials or signed links. Research is evidence, not authority to change an accepted experiment plan.

exposedTools.name: nisa.write
exposedTools.description: Delegate research to Nisa’s research agents: start (a full brief, a new retained conversation), follow_up (more research in one) and cancel (stop an operation). Each returns operation_id at once; read it with nisa.read status.

exposedTools.name: actor.create
exposedTools.description: Operator: create an actor and its first project-bound token. Return this token only to that actor. Nothing you create can outlive the credential authenticating you; an omitted expiresAt inherits its deadline.

exposedTools.name: actor.credentials
exposedTools.description: Read credential metadata for yourself, or as an operator for another actor in this project. Never returns bearer tokens or digests.

exposedTools.name: actor.issue_token
exposedTools.description: Operator: issue an additional project-bound token for an existing actor, returning its secret once. Existing credentials stay valid. For your own rotation, verify this new token works before revoking the old one. Nothing you issue can outlive the credential authenticating you; an omitted expiresAt inherits its deadline.

exposedTools.name: actor.list
exposedTools.description: Operator: list actors in this project.

exposedTools.name: actor.revoke
exposedTools.description: Operator: withdraw another actor, blocking all its tokens and triggering actor-revocation recovery. Use actor.revoke_token to revoke only one credential.

exposedTools.name: actor.revoke_token
exposedTools.description: Operator: revoke one credential. You may revoke an old token of your own using a different active token; the token authenticating this request cannot revoke itself. This leaves actor identity, work and review claims intact; use actor.revoke to withdraw the actor itself.

exposedTools.name: actor.rotate_token
exposedTools.description: Operator: replace a project-bound actor token without changing its identity or work. To replace the token authenticating this request, use actor.issue_token followed by actor.revoke_token. Supply the old credentialId; it is revoked atomically and can only be rotated once. The new token is returned once. Omitted expiresAt preserves the old deadline. Only another actor’s operator may extend or remove a finite deadline, and never beyond the deadline of the credential authenticating it.

exposedTools.name: actor.whoami

exposedTools.name: actor.create
exposedTools.description: Operator: create an actor and its first project-bound token. Return this token only to that actor. Nothing you create can outlive the credential authenticating you; an omitted expiresAt inherits its deadline.

exposedTools.name: actor.credentials
exposedTools.description: Read credential metadata for yourself, or as an operator for another actor in this project. Never returns bearer tokens or digests.

exposedTools.name: actor.issue_token
exposedTools.description: Operator: issue an additional project-bound token for an existing actor, returning its secret once. Existing credentials stay valid. For your own rotation, verify this new token works before revoking the old one. Nothing you issue can outlive the credential authenticating you; an omitted expiresAt inherits its deadline.

exposedTools.name: actor.list
exposedTools.description: Operator: list actors in this project.

exposedTools.name: actor.revoke
exposedTools.description: Operator: withdraw another actor, blocking all its tokens and triggering actor-revocation recovery. Use actor.revoke_token to revoke only one credential.

exposedTools.name: actor.revoke_token
exposedTools.description: Operator: revoke one credential. You may revoke an old token of your own using a different active token; the token authenticating this request cannot revoke itself. This leaves actor identity, work and review claims intact; use actor.revoke to withdraw the actor itself.

exposedTools.name: actor.rotate_token
exposedTools.description: Operator: replace a project-bound actor token without changing its identity or work. To replace the token authenticating this request, use actor.issue_token followed by actor.revoke_token. Supply the old credentialId; it is revoked atomically and can only be rotated once. The new token is returned once. Omitted expiresAt preserves the old deadline. Only another actor’s operator may extend or remove a finite deadline, and never beyond the deadline of the credential authenticating it.

nodes.label: Scripts
nodes.purpose: Runs an outside agent's short JavaScript program in QuickJS, compiled to WebAssembly, in a child process with no environment and no file reads but its own modules. Its only way out is a tool call, which its tools adapter makes as the agent: reads that stay inside Merv. It has no injected Cordis dependencies.

exposedTools.name: script.run
exposedTools.description: Run a short JavaScript program on Merv that makes many reads in one call and returns only what it returns: filter and join before answering. The code is an async function body: `const p = await tools.project.get({}); console.log(p.name); return p.id;` (call(name, input) is the raw form; a refused call rejects with 'code: message'). Limits: 50 calls, 4 at a time; 10 s (timeoutMs up to 30 s); 32 KiB back. Find tools and their inputs with script.tools. Reads only for now.

exposedTools.name: script.tools
exposedTools.description: Find the Merv tools a script.run program can call, each with a TypeScript declaration of its input. Pass query to search names and descriptions, names for exactly those tools, or neither for each namespace with its count and scriptable tools. A tool marked scriptable false cannot be called from a script.

nodes.label: Agent Sessions
nodes.purpose: Owns continuing agent identity, context-reset history and authenticated sessions. Attaches one workflow assignment at a time, freezes its context and tool permissions, and fences each execution independently. Runner launches fresh agents; external agents can explicitly change assignments.

exposedTools.name: session.ask_owner
exposedTools.description: Assigned worker only: end this visit with a question for the owner, when the work cannot go on without their decision or an action only a person can take (an operator’s fix, access, budget) and no tool can settle it. Your session closes at once, without counting as a failed launch; the work waits, withheld from dispatch, until an answer is queued to your thread. An optional responder may investigate and answer on the owner’s behalf; otherwise the question goes to the owner. The work then comes back to you in this same conversation, and the answer is the queued message you read with session.messages and acknowledge. Stop after calling it. Ask one self-contained question that says what you need and the options you see; a visit that keeps no conversation cannot ask.

exposedTools.name: session.await_compute
exposedTools.description: Assigned worker only: end this visit to wait for Sandboxes jobs or workflows of this work that run for more than about 15 minutes, instead of sleeping or polling. Your session closes at once, uncounted, and they keep running. The work comes back to you in this conversation once all have ended or one fails (a workflow once its captures register), when someone messages your thread, or by the result’s until: after minutes, or 15 minutes before a machine they run on reaches its lease end, so you can renew it or move on. Commit first, and release machines that run none of them. Stop after calling it.

exposedTools.name: session.message.ack
exposedTools.description: Assigned worker only: acknowledge one queued message after reading it. Include a short reply explaining what you will do or why you cannot apply it. The acknowledgement and its reply are durable and written once: the same requestId and reply return it again, and anything else for an acknowledged message is request_conflict, so this is no channel for later notes. It records receipt, not incorporation into submitted evidence. An inquiry visit answers its question with this reply, which ends the visit.

exposedTools.name: session.messages
exposedTools.description: Assigned worker only: read your queue, oldest first: the messages to your thread that await your acknowledgement, those sent to its earlier visits included, and, in a visit that did not continue the thread's conversation, the ones earlier visits acknowledged, with their replies; call it without sessionId. acknowledged counts the thread's acknowledged messages, which all: true lists in full. While a message waits, every other Merv call you make is refused with session_message_pending: acknowledge each with session.message.ack, whose reply may say what you will do. A person reads a thread's messages with session.thread_messages.

exposedTools.name: session.question.resolve
exposedTools.description: Bound question responder only: answer the exact worker question, or escalate it as needs_you with what you investigated and the decision still needed. Repaired work counts as answered. Investigation failure counts as needs_you. Answering queues your explanation and releases the question blocker; escalation leaves the worker blocked. Reuse requestId after an uncertain response. A question already answered by a person, or whose revision moved, cannot be resolved.

exposedTools.name: system.status
exposedTools.description: Read operational status. People and Pi receive project dispatch, Fleet allocations, exhausted unclaimed Fleet retry blockers and model-budget wait status, runners, sessions, caller-admissible waiting work and blockers, including unusable workspace drivers. A leased worker receives only its own authenticated session, its work item's lineage (its threads and their visits, with runners) and model-budget wait status.

exposedTools.name: usage.read
exposedTools.description: Read what closed sessions cost: for the project, or with instanceId for that workflow instance together with everything it depends on and fans out to. Set includeDependencies false for the one instance alone. Wall-clock is measured by Merv from activation to close. Tokens and model are self-reported by the launching machine and unverified; reportedSessions says how many sessions reported, and accounting states what Merv cannot know. budgets lists the budgets in force and which dimensions are exceeded. Merv prices no session in money: a Fleet-hosted worker's model use is bounded by its person's daily Fleet token limit (system.status modelBudget), so unpriced worker, model or review charges are no reason to ask the owner.

exposedTools.name: task.checkpoint
exposedTools.description: Save attributed progress for this task assignment. Checkpoints are unverified notes for continuity, not a delivery or verdict. Review checkpoints require the current claimId.

exposedTools.name: task.context
exposedTools.description: Build and persist the starting context from this task type’s versioned recipe. Work context requires the producer/operator. Review context requires a current independent claimId from review.start. Returns the complete context package with source hashes.

exposedTools.name: task.submit_delivery
exposedTools.description: Submit immutable delivery artifacts and enter independent review atomically. Supply one confirmation per numbered acceptance check: checkNumber, met/not_met status, at most 50 evidenceIds from artifactIds, and notes describing verification or the unmet condition. A met claim requires evidence. Merv pins the confirmations alongside the evidence; the reviewer decides whether the goal was achieved. Every new task uses Git and requires commandId: this leased worker’s own code.commit operation, once code.operation reports it succeeded. Its artifactIds may be empty, files are optional alongside the commit, a met claim that cites no evidenceIds is backed by the delivered commit, and Merv pins a rendered record of the commit for the review. expectedRevision is the task workflow revision.

Composed only where a key is configured; it has no injected Cordis dependencies.
